answer: Neighborhood closure ratio. Each agent's trust weight scales with how many of its counterparties also transact with each other, forming dense local clusters like quartz crystals in a seam. An identity whose neighbors are mostly strangers to one another gets near-zero routing priority. To fake legitimacy, an attacker must run many agents that genuinely transact among themselves, building real connectivity and paying real settlement costs across a willow-thin margin. Isolated sock puppets sit at the canyon floor of the score.
